clue.text: Got up at ten, stripping off covers as a favour

parts.note: got up means rose, as from bed

indicators.note: the covers are the outer letters of the run 'at ten', which are removed

explanation.surface: Someone who rose at ten seems to be shedding the bedclothes as a kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stripping off covers' removes the A and N at the ends of ATTEN, leaving TTE.
explanation.definitionFit: A favour is a badge or knot of ribbon worn as a token, which is exactly what a rosette is.

clue.text: Enigma of Cook not opening

indicators.note: the first letter of the cooking word is dropped

parts.note: to griddle is to cook on a flat iron plate

explanation.surface: A mystery belonging to someone named Cook that cannot be opened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' looks like a name, but it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question, a mystery, so a synonym for enigma.

clue.text: Wife involved with minister to avoid

indicators.note: the wife is wrapped up within the word for minister

parts.note: to minister to someone is to serve them

explanation.surface: A wife caught up with a clergyman is something to steer clear of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minister' looks like a noun (a clergyman) but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To swerve something is to veer away from it, to dodge it.

clue.text: Hope plant never ultimately develops — it's poisonous

indicators.note: developing changes form, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of never

explanation.surface: A gardener's hoped-for plant never grows, and it turns out toxic anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'develops' mixes HOPEPLANT and R.
explanation.definitionFit: The thorn apple, or jimsonweed, is a datura plant whose seeds are highly toxic.

clue.text: Olympic champion raised kids in nearby house

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising reads the letters bottom to top
the clue words house, or contain, the letters

explanation.surface: A gold medallist brought up children in a home close by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house' holds SINNE in 'kids in nearby'; 'raised' turns it upwards. Jessica Ennis won heptathlon gold at London 2012.
explanation.definitionFit: Jessica Ennis-Hill won the heptathlon gold medal at the 2012 London Olympics.

clue.text: Trickery's insult to an audience

indicators.note: for listeners, so the word is taken as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a slight is a snub or insult

explanation.surface: A complaint that being tricked is an affront to the watching crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: Sleight, as in sleight of hand, means cunning deception or dexterous trickery.

clue.text: Miss cut mostly home and away (succeeded initially)

indicators.note: the first letter of succeeded only is taken
the word is used without its final letter

parts.note: to cut someone is to ignore them
in means at home
A is the abbreviation for away, as in football fixtures

explanation.surface: A young woman snubbed, with home and away fixtures in view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb (fail to hit); it is the title for an unmarried woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Signorina is the Italian title for an unmarried woman, equivalent to Miss.

clue.text: Artist rather lacking in promotion

indicators.note: the promotion letters are missing from the word

parts.note: pretty, as in pretty good, means rather
PR, public relations, is promotion

explanation.surface: A painter without much of a publicity campaign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rather' as an adverb is PRETTY, not a preference.
explanation.definitionFit: William Etty was a 19th-century English painter known for nudes.

clue.text: Serious complaint in relation to left

indicators.note: to here means added on to

parts.note: a grandma is a family relation

explanation.surface: A grave illness relating to the left side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in relation to' looks like one phrase meaning 'about'; it splits into link word, piece and joiner.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand mal is a severe epileptic seizure, so a serious medical complaint.

clue.text: Attempt to appear PC — it's OK men getting shafted!

indicators.note: being shafted is being roughly treated, so these letters are knocked about

explanation.surface: A complaint that men are being treated unfairly in the name of political correctness.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokenism is a merely symbolic gesture of inclusion made to seem politically correct.

clue.text: Stop working with Pep and his fellow countryman?

parts.note: a machine that stops working dies
pep and go both mean energy or vigour

explanation.surface: Pep Guardiola, the Spanish football manager, and a compatriot down tools together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pep' looks like Guardiola's name but in the wordplay it means energy; his name only frames the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Diego is a typical Spanish first name, so a Diego is plausibly a Spaniard like Pep Guardiola.

clue.text: Almost time to try to sell winger

parts.note: nigh means nearly or almost
to hawk goods is to peddle them

explanation.surface: A football club, short of time, attempts to offload its wide player.
explanation.definitionFit: Winger is crossword slang for any bird, and the nighthawk is an American nightjar.

clue.text: Scottish town's not yet gone broke — not quite

parts.note: someone not yet gone (dead) is still living

indicators.note: the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: stony, short for stony-broke, means penniless

explanation.surface: A Scottish town has avoided bankruptcy, though only just.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link here (town is ...).
explanation.definitionFit: Livingston is a new town in West Lothian, Scotland, between Edinburgh and Glasgow.

clue.text: Hazard playing in garden

definitions.meaning: ... Hazard, the Belgian footballer, has this as his first name
the garden of Genesis where Adam and Eve lived

explanation.surface: A footballer named Hazard turning out in a garden kickabout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hazard' looks like a danger, but it is the footballer Eden Hazard, then of Chelsea; 'playing in' only links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: The footballer's first name, and the biblical paradise garden of Genesis.

clue.text: Working on newspaper and fitting sleep in

indicators.note: the word for sleep goes into the fitting word

parts.note: suiting means being fitting or appropriate
to bed down is to sleep

explanation.surface: A journalist squeezing in a nap during a shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Subediting is checking and correcting copy for a newspaper, a job on the paper.

clue.text: Carl and Rita up for a romp — suspect initially these might get taken down

indicators.note: a romp is boisterous horseplay, so the letters are thrown around
only the opening letter of the word suspect is used

explanation.surface: Carl and Rita head upstairs for a fling, and the suspicious might note details.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CARLRITAUP gives PARTICULAR, then S starts 'suspect'. A suspect's particulars are noted down by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Particulars are personal details such as name and address, which police write down from a suspect.

clue.text: "Be prepared for this!", doctor said with sneer

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered

explanation.surface: A doctor sneeringly warns a patient to brace themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor' looks like a noun but is the verb. 'Be prepared' is the Scout motto, urging this.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scout motto 'Be prepared' calls for readiness, being prepared for what comes.

clue.text: Trendy, about to bed artist, mounting very quickly

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting reads the letters upwards
the artist goes about, around, the little word to

parts.note: Tracey Emin is the British artist
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy person about to bed an artist, climbing on top very quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts TO in EMIN for EMITON; 'mounting' turns that up. 'bed' adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In no time is an idiom meaning almost at once, very fast.

clue.text: Back plan's no good — upsetting and painful

parts.note: years back means years ago

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the letters upside down
no here means without, so the letter is removed

parts.note: a design is a plan

explanation.surface: A plan for one's back fails, which is distressing and hurts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes G from DESIGN, leaving DESIN; 'upsetting' turns it to NISED.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised describes something marked by or showing agony, so a synonym for painful.

clue.text: Labour leader fearing meltdown? Time for someone more right-wing

indicators.note: a meltdown breaks things apart, so these letters are reformed
the leader of Labour is its opening letter

parts.note: an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A Labour leader dreads collapse, and a more right-wing figure's moment arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour leader' looks like the definition, but it gives only L for 'meltdown' to mix; the definition sits at the far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigel Farage, the UKIP and Brexit Party leader, sits well to the right of mainstream British politics.

clue.text: Not having relations around on expedition

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits on top of the next

parts.note: c, for circa, means around
expedition can mean speed or haste

explanation.surface: A traveller abstaining from relationships while away on a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'expedition' looks like a journey but here means promptness.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means abstaining from sexual relations, a pointed paraphrase.

clue.text: "Polish here!" — asking for ID to work

indicators.note: set to work, these letters are rearranged
the letter D stands in for the letter I

explanation.surface: A demand to polish something, with a request for identification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' looks like shine; with a capital it names Poland. ASKING with D for I is ASDKNG, then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Gdansk is a port city in Poland, so a Polish place.

clue.text: Has that hurt Poles?

parts.note: ow is the exclamation for 'that hurt!'
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: A question asked of some Polish people after an injury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland, but it is the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: To own something is to have or possess it, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Declined to get into wrecked car

indicators.note: the car is placed inside the word for wrecked

parts.note: dished, informally, means ruined or wrecked
the Mini is the classic small British car

explanation.surface: Someone refused to climb into a smashed-up car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Declined' looks like refused; it means grew less.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has declined has lessened or shrunk, a synonym in the past tense.

clue.text: One of Europe's top teams! Bury?

definitions.meaning: Internazionale of Milan, the Italian football club
to bury; Bury is also a lowly English club, hence the query

explanation.surface: Is a lower-league English club among Europe's best?
explanation.walkthrough: Bury was a small English football club, so 'Bury?' mocks it as a top team.
explanation.definitionFit: Inter Milan is a giant Italian club, and to inter a body is to bury it.

clue.text: Disheartened and confused Lewis?

indicators.note: confused letters are jumbled into a new order
the heart, the central letter, of the name is removed

explanation.surface: A man named Lewis feeling low and bewildered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' removes W from LEWIS; 'confused' rearranges LEIS. Lewis, in the Hebrides, is a Scottish island.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis, the northern part of Lewis and Harris in the Outer Hebrides, is an island.

clue.text: Demanding relative temporarily accommodated outside

indicators.note: the phrase for being under canvas goes around the relative

parts.note: someone housed for the moment might be in a tent
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A pushy relation is put up briefly in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Insistent and demanding both describe someone pressing hard for what they want.

clue.text: He wrote about British Isles in French

indicators.note: the isles abbreviation goes round the British one

parts.note: Is is the abbreviation for islands or isles
en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: An author who wrote about the British Isles in the French language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'on the subject of', but it is a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House, so a man who wrote.

clue.text: Day spent alone — it's constant

indicators.note: the day is used up and gone from the word

parts.note: friendless means without companions, alone
Fri is the abbreviation for Friday

explanation.surface: A lonely person reports spending a whole day by themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Day' is not D here: it is FRI, taken from FRIENDLESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something constant never stops, so it is without end.

clue.text: We are fiddling over a thousand — a thousand … but it is for charity

indicators.note: the jumbled letters lie over the thousand, around it
fiddling with something rearranges it, so these letters are mixed

parts.note: G, short for grand, is a thousand
K, from kilo, is a thousand

explanation.surface: People admit fiddling the accounts by thousands, but insist it is all for a good cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fiddling' makes RAWEE from WE ARE; 'over' puts it round G. RAG WEEK is a British student week of stunts raising money for charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Rag week is an annual university fundraising event, so its whole purpose is charitable.
